paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness Web UI in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) - converts the whole rendered interface, inc
luding third-party plugin copy, at the DOM layer.
# dsh-zh-tw-ui
繁體中文 | **English**

Renders the **entire DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web UI in Traditional Chinese
(Taiwan)** — DSH's own cop

y, **third-party plugin copy**, and text that later DSH
versions add — by converting the DOM, not by
shipping a language pack.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Because it works at the render layer, it does not have the failure mode that
dictionary-based langua

ge packs have: *uncovered copy falls back to Simplified
Chinese and the UI looks half-translated.*
## The problem

DSH ships exactly two locales: `zh` (Simplified) and `en`. Using DSH in Taiwan
breaks in three place

exactly two locales: `zh` (Simplified) and `en`. Using DSH in Taiwan
breaks in three places at once:

1. **DSH's own UI** is Simplified without a language pack;
2. **third-party plugins** (market, sideb

ar, IM bridges, Agent Teams, …) each ship
[该节后续省略]
## Why not just use another Traditional Chinese plugin?

This is the reason the project exists, so here is the honest version. All figures
were checked on **
2026-10-13** from each package's npm manifest or repo README.
| Option | Mechanism | Covers third-party plugins | Relationship with DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 |
| `@huanlin/dsh-plugin-better-locale` 0.4.3 | registers dictionaries (39 namespaces) | no | peer say

s `^0.1.5-rc.2` (excludes 0.2.x) → needs a manual exact-version exemption to load |
| `@mimateinn/ds
h-i18n` 0.2.6 | dictionaries + Simplified→Traditional character fallback | yes | peer says `<0.2.0-0

` → blocked by the compatibility gate without an exemption |
| `dsh-locale-zh-tw` (npm, 0.1.1) | pat
ches `LocaleRuntime` internals | yes | documents itself against the `dsh-client-locale@0.1.1-rc.2` s

hape; **degrades silently** on mismatch |
| `dsh-multi-lang-ui` 0.1.1 | dictionaries + char table +
DOM fallback | yes | peer has no upper bound, passes the gate — mechanically the closest to this pro

ject |
| `iceice666/dsh-locale-zh-tw` | dictionaries only (50 ns / 1691 strings) | no (by design, pe

r its README) | — |
| **dsh-zh-tw-ui** (this project) | **pure DOM conversion** | yes | **no peer de
pendencies, touches no DSH API** |
Each existing approach has a structural weakness:

1. **Dictionary-based** (better-locale, iceice666) — coverage is frozen at the
upstream version the

pack was built against. Measured on this machine:
better-locale 0.4.3 ships 39 namespaces while DSH

0.2.0-rc.2 registers about 49
core namespaces, and **17 of them have no Traditional dictionary at al

l**
(`pluginManager`, `permission`, `settings.shell`, `settings.webSearch`,
`agent-team`, `voice-inp

ut`, `schedule.manager`, …). Worse, its fallback chain
is `zh-TW → zh → en`, so the gaps render in *

*Simplified, not English** — which
is exactly why a language pack can look like "it installed but no

thing
happened".
2. **Core-patching** (the npm `dsh-locale-zh-tw`) — tightly coupled to DSH
internal

s and *designed* to degrade silently: after a DSH update it can simply
stop doing anything, without

o degrade silently: after a DSH update it can simply
stop doing anything, without an error.
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- Engine: **OpenCC `cn → twp`** (Simplified → Traditional with Taiwan vocabulary):
设置→設定, 网络→網路, 软件→

軟體, 文件夹→資料夾, 服务器→伺服器, 内存→記憶體,
屏幕→螢幕, 鼠标→滑鼠, 保存→儲存, 搜索→搜尋, 插件→外掛.
- A small override table (`DEFAULT_

OVERRIDES` in `src/convert.mjs`) fixes wording
OpenCC misses or renders in a non-Taiwan way: 只讀→唯讀,

超時→逾時, 反饋→回饋,
獲取→取得, 許可權→權限.
- `<html lang>` is set to `zh-Hant-TW` so the browser picks Taiwan glyp

h forms.
- Memoised per text node, non-Han strings short-circuit, and values are only
written when t

hey actually change — the converter also remembers its own writes,
so it can never ping-pong with Re

actually change — the converter also remembers its own writes,
so it can never ping-pong with React.
## Safety boundary: what is never converted
| Target | Behaviour |
| `<code>` `<pre>` `<kbd>` `<samp>` `<var>`, CodeMirror / Monaco / xterm / ace / syntax highlighting

| **subtree and attributes untouched** |
| `<input>` `<textarea>` `<select>` `<option>` | only `pla

ceholder` / `title`; **what you type or pick is untouched** |
| `contenteditable` (including rich-te

xt composers) | untouched |
| `<svg>` `<math>`, `<script>` `<style>` `<canvas>` `<iframe>` `<video>`

`<audio>` | untouched |
| anything marked `data-zh-tw-skip` or `translate="no"` | untouched |
| str
ings without Han characters (English, kana, digits, code) | passed through |

In other words: **code is never rewritten**, and copying code behaves exactly as
before.
## Limitations
An honest list. All of these follow from the display-layer design:

1. **The screen changes; the data does not.** Stored text, what the model
receives, and what is writ

ten to files stay as they were.
- Copying **code**: unaffected (code blocks are excluded).
- Copying

**prose**: you get Traditional, because the copy comes from the screen.
- Your own message bubble r

enders in Traditional, but the model still receives
exactly what you typed.
2. **Text painted into a

canvas is not converted** (charts, image editors,
self-drawn components).
3. **Cross-origin iframe

content is not converted** (same-origin iframes are).
4. **Wording can be contextually wrong.** Open

CC is a phrase table; occasional
mismatches happen (proper nouns especially). Tune the override tabl

e or mark
the region with `data-zh-tw-skip`.
5. **There is a performance cost.** Every text node cos

ts a dictionary lookup.
Memoisation, the non-Han short circuit, and only touching added/changed node

s
keep it small, but very long conversations or huge list pages may show a slight
delay.
6. **It is

not a language pack.** No "繁體中文" entry appears in DSH's Language
list. If you switch DSH to English

there is no Chinese on screen to convert, so
the effect is "nothing happened".
7. **Web/desktop clie

nts only** — TUI and headless have no DOM.
8. **A linked install can be pruned.** If installing anot

her plugin from the
market later triggers pnpm to re-resolve `node_modules`, the link may disappear

(the plugin stops working; DSH itself is unaffected). Re-run
`node install.mjs`.
9. **Native chrome

is out of scope**: DSH Desktop's native menus, tray, and other
non-web UI.
